title: Bilateral grip-change discordance gives a small but training-uncertain arthritis prediction gain across NHANES samples
abstract: Bilateral grip-change discordance produced a small transferred Brier gain (0.00022377, 0.116%) for self-reported arthritis, but the source-target refit interval includes zero; incremental prediction was not established. Models trained on 2953 NHANES2011–2012 adults aged40+ were transferred without target fitting to 3243 NHANES2013–2014 adults. Target weighted Brier loss changed 0.19369779 to 0.19347402; conditional target-PSU95% gain interval [0.00010489766779248629, 0.0003328779042481955], full preprocessing source-target-PSU refit interval [-0.0006577637216108315, 0.0006629791983155717]. The comparator included flexible strength, asymmetry, variability, mean trend, anthropometry, demographics and hand symptoms. This is not a hand-arthritis diagnostic study and does not establish equivalence or clinical utility.
